key_insight: One resident base plus 1-bit sign masks with per-row scales, fused into the matmul, cuts each extra full fine-tune to ~1/16 of a copy.
killer_doubt: This is BitDelta. A 1/16 mask (~1 GB for an 8B model) is larger than a rank-16 LoRA (~40 MB). Most tenants already use LoRA, so the gain over current practice is ~1x.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. At most, compare BitDelta with multi-LoRA serving 100 tenants of an 8B model: HBM per tenant, tokens/s and quality.
prior_art: BitDelta (Liu et al. 2024), DeltaZip, Delta-CoMe; S-LoRA, Punica, vLLM multi-LoRA. Same as R29 I-02143 (DROP) [training knowledge].

key_insight: A CI harness that measures RSS before and after each patch to widely deployed infrastructure would make memory savings a measured quantity rather than a claimed one.
killer_doubt: Postgres, Redis and Kafka RSS is mostly operator-sized buffers and data (shared_buffers, maxmemory, page cache), not code overhead. Patchable slack is likely <5%, and benchmark-specific patches can game the bounty.
decisive_experiment: For 10 of the packages at default and production configs, split RSS into configured buffers or data versus allocator, metadata and fragmentation overhead. If overhead is <5%, drop. About $30k.
prior_art: Chrome PartitionAlloc and Memory Saver work, Gitcoin and bug-bounty funds; same family as R27 I-02295 (DROP) [training knowledge].

key_insight: If fine-tunes freeze the bottom k layers, those layers' prefix KV is bit-identical to the base model's, so it can be shared exactly across all variants.
killer_doubt: DroidSpeak (NSDI'26) already shares cross-variant KV with no freezing rule and recomputes only ~10% of layers. Activated LoRA shares the whole prefix. Duplicated cross-variant prefix KV is a small slice of serving memory.
decisive_experiment: Train 10 LoRA variants of an 8B base, bottom-half frozen versus all layers. On multi-agent shared-prefix traces, compare quality and KV saved against DroidSpeak and aLoRA.
prior_art: DroidSpeak, Microsoft/UChicago, NSDI 2026 (via search snippet); IBM Activated LoRA (2025) [training knowledge]; vLLM prefix cache keyed per adapter.

key_insight: Recommender embedding tables are TB-scale. Computing rows from multi-hash codes through a small MLP, and caching only the hot ~1% exactly, could cut them 10-100x.
killer_doubt: This is DHE plus hybrid caching, both published. Each lookup becomes ~1-10 MFLOP of MLP instead of a ~256 B read, which across thousands of IDs per sample multiplies inference compute 10-100x. Production keeps quantized and hashed tables.
decisive_experiment: On MLPerf DLRM-DCNv2 / Criteo-1TB, compare hybrid DHE with int4 rows plus Unified Embedding: AUC, FLOPs per sample, p99 latency and DRAM. About $50k of GPU time.
prior_art: Deep Hash Embedding (Kang et al., KDD 2021); MP-Rec hybrid table/DHE (Gupta et al., 2023); Google Unified Embedding (NeurIPS 2023); TT-Rec; R28 I-00749 (DROP).

key_insight: A page-table entry type that names a generator kernel and parameters would let a near-memory engine synthesize lines on read, so the memory bound becomes description length rather than raw size.
killer_doubt: Little live DRAM is cheaply generable at 64 B granularity. Zero pages, ~10-20% of swapped pages at Meta, are already deduped. DHE rows need a full MLP per row, and software can simply compute instead of load.
decisive_experiment: Snapshot 5 production-like workloads. Classify pages that a generator under 1 KB can reproduce (constant, strided, PRNG, affine). If they are under 5% beyond zero pages, drop. About $40k.
prior_art: Zero-content augmented caches (Dusser 2009), KSM zero-page merging, Random123 seed regeneration; R33 I-07662 (DROP) [training knowledge].

key_insight: AI racks carry about as much host DRAM as HBM (GB300 NVL72 ~17 TB LPDDR5X vs ~21 TB HBM). Leasing the idle part frees already-installed bits with no new chips.
killer_doubt: No operator data shows how much is idle. Inference nodes now use host DRAM as the KV tier (Dynamo KVBM, LMCache), and a 200-400 Gb/s frontend NIC shared with storage limits harvest bandwidth. Multi-tenant isolation is a blocker.
decisive_experiment: Collect 30 days of per-node host-memory telemetry (RSS, page cache, KV-tier use) from 2 GPU-cloud partners for training and inference. Then run a 16-node RDMA-harvest pilot that measures GPU-job interference. About $150k.
prior_art: Infiniswap (NSDI'17), Fastswap, Microsoft Pond, Kove SDM and MemVerge software pooling, Liqid/UnifabriX/SK hynix Niagara CXL pools. No idle-fraction data found (via search snippet).

key_insight: WebGraph gap and zeta coding cuts adjacency to a few bits per edge. A line-rate decoder would remove the decompression cost.
killer_doubt: Software already does this. GBBS/Ligra+ process the 128B-edge Hyperlink2012 graph on one 1 TB server, and SpZip (MICRO'21) adds hardware decompression. Graph analytics is a small share of DRAM, so the decoder adds <1.5x.
decisive_experiment: Model a near-memory decoder against GBBS compressed-graph software on a 1 TB server for BFS, PageRank and CC, using a SpZip-style simulator. If the speedup is under 1.5x, drop. About $40k.
prior_art: WebGraph (Boldi-Vigna 2004), Ligra+ (DCC 2015), GBBS (SPAA 2018), SpZip (Yang, Emer, Sanchez, MICRO 2021) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Rank/select and Elias-Fano units in the controller could fold the 2-3 dependent accesses of a succinct traversal into one memory round trip, so near-entropy layouts work for general pointer data.
killer_doubt: Software select with BMI2 pdep/tzcnt is already ~10-30 ns. Real indexes and graphs are already compressed (Lucene PFOR, delta CSR), so the extra DRAM saving is more like 1.5-2x than 3-10x.
decisive_experiment: Build a CXL FPGA card with rank/select and Elias-Fano engines. Run succinct trie, graph and inverted-index traversal against BMI2 host software and compressed-CSR baselines, measuring ns per hop and bytes per edge. About $200k.
prior_art: SDSL/sux succinct libraries, FM-index FPGA accelerators, SpZip. Same mechanism as R34 I-05348 (HOLD) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Embedding rows computed from hash codes by a small MLP on tensor cores, rather than stored, could cut recommender embedding DRAM 10x or more.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-06735, with no hot-ID cache. Pure DHE at billions of IDs loses accuracy, and its ~1-10 MFLOP per lookup multiplies inference compute 10-100x, which is why production has not adopted it.
decisive_experiment: Same as I-06735: DHE against quantized and hashed tables on MLPerf DLRM-DCNv2. Measure AUC, FLOPs per sample, latency and DRAM.
prior_art: Deep Hash Embedding (KDD 2021), TT-Rec (MLSys 2021), MP-Rec; dup of I-06735 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Swapping stored ID rows for k-hash codes plus a shared MLP, and keeping exact rows only for the hottest 1%, trades DRAM for compute.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-06735 and published DHE. The hot cache is MP-Rec's hybrid. Compute rises 10-100x per lookup, and production prefers int4 rows plus collision hashing.
decisive_experiment: Same as I-06735: DHE against quantized and hashed tables on MLPerf DLRM-DCNv2. Measure AUC, FLOPs per sample, latency and DRAM.
prior_art: Deep Hash Embedding (KDD 2021); MP-Rec (2023); dup of I-06735 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Multi-hash collision tables with a tiny per-ID sign or scale can shrink embedding tables by large factors while still separating most colliding IDs.
killer_doubt: This is the hashing trick plus hash embeddings with importance weights, both long published. Recommender teams treat ~0.1% AUC as material, and 100x collisions cost more than that, so production stops near 2-10x.
decisive_experiment: Sweep the compression ratio (2x to 100x) for hash embeddings with per-ID weights against ROBE and QR on Criteo-1TB, and find the ratio where AUC loss reaches 0.1%. About $20k.
prior_art: Weinberger hashing trick (2009), Svenstrup hash embeddings (2017), QR trick (2020), ROBE, Google Unified Embedding [training knowledge].

key_insight: Keep KV as a time pyramid: recent tokens at full resolution, older spans pooled into HBM summaries, full copies on flash recalled when attention mass lands on a summary.
killer_doubt: Flash random reads take ~50-100 us against a 20-50 ms decode step. With spread attention, each layer and head triggers recalls, and KV-retrieval systems already do summary plus recall from CPU memory.
decisive_experiment: Fork vLLM with pooled summaries in HBM and full KV on NVMe. On RULER and LongBench at 128k-1M tokens, measure recalls per step, stall time and accuracy against ShadowKV and InfLLM. About $60k.
prior_art: InfLLM, ArkVale (NeurIPS'24), ShadowKV, RetrievalAttention, Quest, Landmark attention; R11 I-04022 (DROP) [training knowledge].
